sourceShortSummaries: Four dragonets introduce their friendships, talents, and private frustrations on the Circular Island before the Jubilee.
sourceLongSummaries: Eight immense statues shelter distinct dragonet communities on the Circular Island, whose annual Jubilee brings them together. Little Tony hears objects clamoring for attention and finds quiet on the Wanderer's palm; he recruits his friend Sculpit into a fictitious-girlfriend story to discourage Glenda, his infatuated former seagull familiar. Sculpit prefers coaching performers to taking the spotlight and needs costume materials for his star client. In the Dark Lady's neighborhood, Zeno pitches names for a comedy club while Heska quietly pranks him. Heska is a skilled hunter who feeds the community, famously catching a giant fiddler crab, while Little Tony prizes unusual finds, including an award-winning butt-shaped pebble.

sourceShortSummaries: Xena demands dazzling jewelry and insists that the reluctant Heska join her Jubilee performance.
sourceLongSummaries: During preparations at the central temple, Sculpit's star performer Xena panics about her costume and suddenly wants a duet partner. Both a gifted singer and aerial acrobat, she expects striking jewelry rather than Little Tony's subtly distinguished pebbles. She confides to her clutchmate Zeno that Heska's famous crab hunt impressed her, then presents recruiting him as her brother's idea. Sculpit tries to steady her and shape a workable performance. Heska ducks away when she calls him and resists performing publicly, but finally agrees to accompany the others somewhere less crowded to demonstrate his flying.

sourceShortSummaries: Sculpit coaches Heska through a successful whip-catching rehearsal and helps turn it into a duet with Xena.
Little Tony trades Edmund to Zare for jewelry after finding an unusually harmonious team of gems for Xena.
sourceLongSummaries: Away from the crowd, Sculpit uses an Unseen Servant carrying a small object to draw Heska into a hunting demonstration. Heska first misses with his whip but catches the object with a claw; after Sculpit's advice and a second attempt with advantage, he executes the catch cleanly, flips the object into the air, and lands with it in hand. Xena, secretly watching from the bushes, bursts out in admiration, making Heska's silver highlights turn red. They develop a routine in which she drops costume pieces for him to catch. Xena keeps Heska and Sculpit rehearsing and sends Little Tony and Zeno to obtain suitable jewelry.

Zeno brings Little Tony to his tailor and collector friend Zare's festival stall. A natural twenty lets Little Tony distinguish the individual voices of the displayed gems, which favor an eight-sided ruby as the centerpiece of a team. When Zare asks for payment, he recognizes Little Tony and eagerly asks about the prizewinning butt-shaped pebble. Little Tony produces Edmund and agrees to the exchange only after Zare promises to care for him. Edmund's closing perspective places the exchange within his ancient history as a statue fragment. Zare offers five pieces of jewelry, adds a few extras out of gratitude, and the pair returns to the others with the collection.

sourceShortSummaries: The Jubilee opens with a ceremony of unity, followed by a disastrous duet that Xena salvages after Heska's whip strikes her.
Zeno defeats Rosca in two rounds of a call-and-response contest and celebrates with his friends.
sourceLongSummaries: The eight communities gather at sunset as their elders place blessed objects in a circle and the egg clutches are honored. The eldest Brightface elder leads the call of eight homes and eight roads, answered by one family. Sculpit encourages Xena and Zeno bolsters Heska, then Xena launches into a brilliant aerial performance. Heska rolls three ones, strikes her with his whip instead of catching the falling jewelry, and hides in a Fog Cloud. Xena rises from the fog and wins back the crowd with a triumphant pose while Heska escapes. He blames his friends for involving him; afterward, Xena says she will never forgive him, calls him cute, and kisses his cheek.

The group encounters Rosca and his crew at the Jubilee's music and dance circle, where Zeno's friendly archrival challenges him. Sculpit offers encouragement and Bardic Inspiration. Zeno wins the opening round with a strong performance and uses Sick Burn to reduce Rosca's response. Rosca escalates to props in round two; Heska tries to disrupt his act but fails, and Rosca successfully retrieves a fake egg for his rhyme. Zeno answers with a verse naming Heska, Little Tony, and Sculpit, earning an extra performance bonus and winning decisively. Rosca concedes, embraces him, and the crowd pulls the whole group into the celebration.

sourceShortSummaries: The friends share a meal above the festival until silence, music, wild magic, and a moving shadow interrupt them.
The group follows Little Tony's silence and Zeno's inner note to a glowing object above the Wanderer's palm.
Unable to open or read the egg, the dragonets discover that touching it evokes home and begins to illuminate its engravings.
Embracing the egg gives the four dragonets a shared vision and briefly heightened abilities before the Wanderer's eye lights blue.
sourceLongSummaries: At an overlook above the temple grounds, Heska eats trout he caught himself and vows never to perform again. Little Tony enjoys roasted lobsters, Zeno relives his victory while eating fish meatballs, and Sculpit offers an elaborate seafood dish while regretting that he gave Heska too little coaching. Their conversation turns to future performances and Zeno's club. As Little Tony addresses a passing cloud, all the objects' voices abruptly fall silent for him. Zeno hears an exceptionally beautiful note in his mind, Sculpit involuntarily teleports about twenty feet along the direction of the Wanderer statue, and Heska spots an unnatural movement in the sky. The festival below otherwise appears normal.

Heska flies up after the moving shadow, and the others follow. Little Tony finds that the silence has direction, while Zeno's inner note grows louder or softer as he changes course; humming along brings Zeno a fleeting sense of peace. Watching from above, Heska notices their movements converging. They compare impressions, identify the Wanderer as their destination, and fly toward it. A large glow hovers over the outstretched palm. As they approach, the glow fades, Little Tony hears the surrounding objects again, and Zeno's note stops. The object remains, and the group lands beside it.

On the Wanderer's palm, Heska knocks on the egg with Mage Hand and tests it with his whip; its unfamiliar material resembles neither ordinary stone nor metal. Sculpit recognizes its precise geometric engravings as similar to patterns near the island's ruins. Zeno's Detect Thoughts finds nothing, although the shell might block the spell, and Heska finds no opening. Little Tony touches the egg, welcomes it, and hears the word home in his mind. His sincere embrace brings an overwhelming sense of belonging and makes nearby engravings glow. Heska also feels moved when touching it and nuzzles against it, while Little Tony calls everyone to join in a hug.

The four embrace the egg, lighting eight points and merging their consciousness into a shared vision. They experience a dying older purple dragonet beneath burning skies and fading lights, then become the light that envelops it. A sense of home accompanies images of a man with a jade hand, familiar companions, and the Circular Island, followed by passage through impossible geometry and the surrounding storm to the Wanderer's palm. They awaken beside the darkening egg. For a few minutes, Little Tony can select individual objects' voices across the island, Zeno senses music suited to trees, rivers, animals, and wind, Heska feels precise bodily control and hunting prowess, and Sculpit feels mastery over his wild magic. These sensations disappear, and the closing view shows the Wanderer's eye shining blue.

sourceEntries.longSummary: Away from the crowd, Sculpit uses an Unseen Servant carrying a small object to draw Heska into a hunting demonstration. Heska first misses with his whip but catches the object with a claw; after Sculpit's advice and a second attempt with advantage, he executes the catch cleanly, flips the object into the air, and lands with it in hand. Xena, secretly watching from the bushes, bursts out in admiration, making Heska's silver highlights turn red. They develop a routine in which she drops costume pieces for him to catch. Xena keeps Heska and Sculpit rehearsing and sends Little Tony and Zeno to obtain suitable jewelry.

Zare offers five pieces of jewelry, adds a few extras out of gratitude, and the pair returns to the others with the collection.

recapBlocks.title: Triumphs and Disasters at the Jubilee
sourceShortSummaries: The Jubilee opens with a ceremony of unity, followed by a disastrous duet that Xena salvages after Heska's whip strikes her.
Zeno defeats Rosca in two rounds of a call-and-response contest and celebrates with his friends.
sourceLongSummaries: The eight communities gather at sunset as their elders place blessed objects in a circle and the egg clutches are honored. The eldest Brightface elder leads the call of eight homes and eight roads, answered by one family. Sculpit encourages Xena and Zeno bolsters Heska, then Xena launches into a brilliant aerial performance. Heska rolls three ones, strikes her with his whip instead of catching the falling jewelry, and hides in a Fog Cloud. Xena rises from the fog and wins back the crowd with a triumphant pose while Heska escapes. He blames his friends for involving him; afterward, Xena says she will never forgive him, calls him cute, and kisses his cheek.

The group encounters Rosca and his crew at the Jubilee's music and dance circle, where Zeno's friendly archrival challenges him. Sculpit offers encouragement and Bardic Inspiration. Zeno wins the opening round with a strong performance and uses Sick Burn to reduce Rosca's response. Rosca escalates to props in round two; Heska tries to disrupt his act but fails, and Rosca successfully retrieves a fake egg for his rhyme. Zeno answers with a verse naming Heska, Little Tony, and Sculpit, earning an extra performance bonus and winning decisively. Rosca concedes, embraces him, and the crowd pulls the whole group into the celebration.

recapBlocks.title: Dinner and the Strange Silence
sourceShortSummaries: The friends share a meal above the festival until silence, music, wild magic, and a moving shadow interrupt them.
The group follows Little Tony's silence and Zeno's inner note to a glowing object above the Wanderer's palm.
sourceLongSummaries: At an overlook above the temple grounds, Heska eats trout he caught himself and vows never to perform again. Little Tony enjoys roasted lobsters, Zeno relives his victory while eating fish meatballs, and Sculpit offers an elaborate seafood dish while regretting that he gave Heska too little coaching. Their conversation turns to future performances and Zeno's club. As Little Tony addresses a passing cloud, all the objects' voices abruptly fall silent for him. Zeno hears an exceptionally beautiful note in his mind, Sculpit involuntarily teleports about twenty feet along the direction of the Wanderer statue, and Heska spots an unnatural movement in the sky. The festival below otherwise appears normal.

Heska flies up after the moving shadow, and the others follow. Little Tony finds that the silence has direction, while Zeno's inner note grows louder or softer as he changes course; humming along brings Zeno a fleeting sense of peace. Watching from above, Heska notices their movements converging. They compare impressions, identify the Wanderer as their destination, and fly toward it. A large glow hovers over the outstretched palm. As they approach, the glow fades, Little Tony hears the surrounding objects again, and Zeno's note stops. The object remains, and the group lands beside it.

recapBlocks.title: The Egg and the Meaning of Home
sourceShortSummaries: Unable to open or read the egg, the dragonets discover that touching it evokes home and begins to illuminate its engravings.
Embracing the egg gives the four dragonets a shared vision and briefly heightened abilities before the Wanderer's eye lights blue.
sourceLongSummaries: On the Wanderer's palm, Heska knocks on the egg with Mage Hand and tests it with his whip; its unfamiliar material resembles neither ordinary stone nor metal. Sculpit recognizes its precise geometric engravings as similar to patterns near the island's ruins. Zeno's Detect Thoughts finds nothing, although the shell might block the spell, and Heska finds no opening. Little Tony touches the egg, welcomes it, and hears the word home in his mind. His sincere embrace brings an overwhelming sense of belonging and makes nearby engravings glow. Heska also feels moved when touching it and nuzzles against it, while Little Tony calls everyone to join in a hug.

The four embrace the egg, lighting eight points and merging their consciousness into a shared vision. They experience a dying older purple dragonet beneath burning skies and fading lights, then become the light that envelops it. A sense of home accompanies images of a man with a jade hand, familiar companions, and the Circular Island, followed by passage through impossible geometry and the surrounding storm to the Wanderer's palm. They awaken beside the darkening egg. For a few minutes, Little Tony can select individual objects' voices across the island, Zeno senses music suited to trees, rivers, animals, and wind, Heska feels precise bodily control and hunting prowess, and Sculpit feels mastery over his wild magic. These sensations disappear, and the closing view shows the Wanderer's eye shining blue.
